extraction_sources: Dressing the Man - Alan Flusser - Chapter 3: Proportion
FashionBeans - How to Dress for Your Body Shape
The Modest Man - How to Dress for Your Body Type
The VOU - Men's Body Shapes ALL 7

parameters.name: body_shape
parameters.description: Primary geometric classification of male body silhouette based on relative proportions of shoulders, chest, waist, and hips

values.definition: Broad shoulders and chest with gentle taper through waist, hips, and legs. Well-proportioned. The 'ideal' or 'Vitruvian' male shape — most clothing is designed for this.
Chest and shoulders significantly broader than waist and hips. Narrow lower body relative to upper. Top-heavy V-shaped torso. Chest measures 8+ inches more than waist.
Shoulders roughly same width as waist and hips. Minimal natural taper. Usually lean/slim. Straight up-and-down silhouette.
Larger around the waist and hips than shoulders. Sloping shoulders. Weight carried in midsection. Narrower up top, wider below.
Round at the centre of the body. Prominent middle. Shoulders and lower legs appear slimmer by comparison. Weight concentrated in torso/belly.
Well-developed midsection with average shoulders. Similar to oval but with more defined shoulders. Common in middle-aged men.
Narrow shoulders that slope down, with wider hips. Pear-shaped. Less common in men.

parameters.notes: Flusser does not use geometric shape names. He categorizes by height + build combinations (short/heavy, short/slim, tall, athletic). The geometric taxonomy from FashionBeans and The VOU is more systematic for a recommendation engine. Both systems map to each other.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Overall vertical stature of the man

values.definition: Below 5'7" (170cm). Legs proportionally short relative to torso. Primary goal: create illusion of greater height.
5'7" to 6'0" (170-183cm). Standard proportions. Most clothing designed for this range.
Above 6'0" (183cm). Needs full-proportioned clothing. Goal: produce more horizontal lines to counterbalance vertical dominance.

parameters.name: build
parameters.description: Overall mass and musculature of the frame

values.definition: Lean, narrow frame. Closely fitted clothes accentuate narrowness. Should dress 'large' — add visual breadth and structure.
Moderate frame. Neither notably thin nor heavy. Standard fit clothing works well.
Chest measures 8+ inches more than waist. Exaggerated V-shaped torso. Broad shoulders and chest, narrow waist. Goal: balance upper and lower halves.
Broad and solid but not necessarily overweight. Short and wide frame. Compact.
Prominent middle, significant girth. Should dress 'large' with straight-hanging lines. Close-fitting clothes reveal more than they conceal.

parameters.name: torso_vs_leg_ratio
parameters.description: Relative length of torso compared to legs. Flusser notes most short men are short because their legs are proportionally short relative to their torso.

values.definition: Torso is proportionally long relative to legs. Common in shorter men. Jacket length must be kept short to create illusion of longer legs.
Torso and legs are proportionally balanced. Standard clothing proportions work.
Legs are proportionally long relative to torso. Common in tall men. Can wear longer jackets.

parameters.name: shoulder_width
parameters.description: Width of the shoulders relative to the frame. Flusser: 'As its widest dimension, the shoulder sets the mood for the rest of the jacket.'

values.definition: Shoulders narrower than hips or proportionally small. Requires building out with padding or structured jackets.
Shoulders proportional to the frame. Standard jacket shoulders work.
Shoulders significantly wider than waist. Dominant feature. Jacket shoulders should be soft and natural-looking to avoid exaggerating width.

parameters.name: shoulder_slope
parameters.description: Angle of the shoulders from neck to arm

values.definition: Shoulders angle downward noticeably. May need slight padding to square up. Flusser: unless extremely slope-shouldered, avoid built-up shoulders.
Standard slight downward slope. Natural-shoulder jacket works well (e.g., Brooks Brothers).
Shoulders form near-right angles. Avoid additional padding. 90-degree angles bracketing the head emphasize shortness.

parameters.name: face_shape
parameters.description: Shape of the face — determines collar and neckwear choices. Flusser: 'Think of the face as a picture and the collar as its frame.'

values.definition: Smaller face with fine features. Requires collar of restrained dimensions. Smaller-scale accessories.
Standard proportions. Standard collar widths and scales work.
Broader, larger face. Wider head. Requires correspondingly larger collar. Jacket shoulders may need building up to offset wider head.
Narrow, elongated face. Narrower collar. Sloped, narrow shoulders harmonize with thinner face.

parameters.name: neck
parameters.description: Neck height/length and thickness — affects collar choices

values.definition: Short neck. Lower collar heights. Avoid high collars that crowd the neck.
Standard neck length. Standard collar heights work.
Long neck. Can accommodate taller collars. More room for collar-tie interplay.
Thick, broad neck. Often accompanies athletic build. Vertical-pointing collars (tabs, straight points) help elongate.

parameters.name: arm_length
parameters.description: Relative arm length — affects jacket sleeve and shirt cuff proportions

values.definition: Short arms relative to torso. Half inch of shirt cuff showing is sufficient.
Standard arm length. Jacket sleeve finishes at wrist bone.
Long arms. 3/4 to 1 inch of shirt cuff should show below jacket for better proportion. (Flusser cites Gary Cooper as example.)

parameters.name: waist_definition
parameters.description: How defined or prominent the waist/midsection is

values.definition: Clear waist taper. Can wear more fitted, waist-suppressed clothing.
Some waist definition. Standard fit works.
Minimal waist indentation — straight from chest to hip. Rectangle body. Needs clothing that creates waist illusion.
Midsection is widest point. Oval/triangle body. Needs straight-hanging clothes, trousers on natural waist. Close-fitting clothes 'create the look of a stuffed sausage' (Flusser).

parameters.name: chest_to_waist_drop
parameters.description: Difference between chest and waist measurements. Key indicator for body shape classification.

values.definition: Less than 4 inches difference. Rectangle or oval body. Straight silhouette.
4-7 inches difference. Trapezoid body. Natural taper.
8+ inches difference. Athletic/inverted triangle. Flusser defines athletic as 'chest measures eight inches or more than waist.'

parameters.name: foot_size
parameters.description: Size of feet relative to frame — affects trouser bottom width and shoe choices

values.definition: Smaller feet relative to frame. Wide trouser bottoms make small feet appear even smaller. Need proportional shoe/trouser balance.
Proportional to the frame. Standard trouser-to-shoe proportions work.
Large feet relative to frame. Narrow trouser bottoms make large feet loom even larger. Heavier men need larger footwear to counterpoint volume above.

parameters.name: posture
parameters.description: Natural standing posture — affects how jackets hang and sleeves fall

values.definition: Carries arms or body forward. Sleeves may not lie smoothly — need rotation. Collar may stand away from neck.
Standard upright posture. Clothing hangs as designed.
Very erect posture. May cause collar to sit differently. Stand naturally during fitting, 'not as if you had just graduated West Point' (Flusser).

parameters.name: shoulder_vs_hip_ratio
parameters.description: Relative width of shoulders to hips — primary determinant of body shape

values.definition: Shoulders significantly wider than hips. V-shape or inverted triangle. Upper body dominant.
Shoulders and hips roughly equal width. Rectangle or trapezoid.
Hips wider than shoulders. Triangle or trapezium shape. Less common in men.

parameters.name: head_size
parameters.description: Size of head relative to shoulders — affects jacket shoulder proportions

values.definition: Smaller head. Overly wide shoulders will make head appear disproportionately small.
Head proportional to frame. Standard shoulder width works.
Wider/larger head. Too-narrow shoulders make head appear larger. May need slightly built-up shoulders to offset.

optical_correction_principles.description: North-and-south lines stretch out and narrow the physique. Stripes, long lapels, creases, and monochrome dressing create vertical emphasis.
East-and-west lines add width. Belts, cuffs, contrasting top/bottom, checks, and pocket flaps create horizontal emphasis.
Darker colors recede and make areas appear smaller/thinner. Medium-to-dark register for stout physiques.
Lighter colors advance and make areas appear larger. Thin men can wear lighter colors to advantage.
One color from top to bottom creates an unbroken vertical line, making the figure appear taller and slimmer. 'The suit's ultimate color lesson' for short/heavy men.
Pronounced contrast between upper and lower halves divides the figure, shortening apparent height. Height-challenged men should avoid this.
Pattern scale should harmonize with body type. Narrow-to-medium stripes for thin physique; slightly broader, less pronounced lines for fuller figure. Tall men can wear larger-scaled patterns.
Smooth-faced fabrics such as fine worsteds minimize bulk and thickness.
Heavier, textured fabrics (flannels, cheviots, tweeds) add visual weight. Good for thin frames, avoid for heavy frames.
Slanting/diagonal lines minimize girth. The double-breasted jacket's asymmetrical lapels lead the eye away from center of torso.
Pocket flaps, ticket pockets, turn-back sleeve cuffs inject 'stylish clutter' that impedes long vertical sweeps. Useful for tall men.

flusser_five_intersections.description: Flusser identifies five major body intersections where proportion rules apply. Each contains a network of lines and curves that, when correctly connected, enhance the overall aesthetic.

intersections.name: neck
key_elements: collar shape relative to face shape
collar height relative to neck length
tie knot size relative to collar spread
intersections.flusser_rule: Face is a picture, collar is its frame. Small face = restrained collar. Larger face = correspondingly larger collar.

intersections.name: shoulder
key_elements: shoulder width relative to head size
lapel width relative to shoulder breadth
intersections.flusser_rule: Shoulders frame the head. Too narrow = head appears larger. Too wide = head appears smaller. Broad shoulders need fuller lapels for balance.

intersections.name: waist
intersections.flusser_rule: Waist button is the fulcrum — should sit 1/2 inch below natural waist. Must divide body so torso and legs appear at maximum length.

intersections.name: wrist
intersections.flusser_rule: Jacket sleeve should finish at wrist bone. 1/2 to 1 inch of shirt cuff must show. Sleeves should taper from shoulder to wrist — no flapping.

intersections.name: ankle
intersections.flusser_rule: Trouser bottom should cover about two-thirds of the shoe. Width must harmonize with shoe scale. Narrow bottoms + large feet = feet loom larger.
